document.abstract: Some of the difficulties attending the taking and projection of motion pictures in actual colors are briefly discussed, particular attention being paid to the need of matching the taking and projecting lights spectrally. The author concludes that, despite the great amount of research work being done in emulsions, optics, etc., little will be accomplished in achieving motion pictures in natural colors unless the same particular care be taken with the light sources.
